title: West Town Cross-Street, 02:14
html:
**Setting:** West Town sector, narrow cross-street near The Pivot. Wet asphalt, parked cars, a concrete planter, a dumpster. Rain stopped 40 minutes ago â€” TENG film at reduced efficiency (~45%). Night.

**Gang:** - Mira (captain, chrome jaw, BCI implant, machine pistol) - KT (augmented left arm elbow-to-fingertip, machete in right hand) - Rook (heavy, augmented legs, body armor, heavy pistol) - Nines (on a fire escape above, rifle) - Dex (unaugmented flanker, two handguns) - The Dog (quadruped combat drone, pit bull-sized, jaw-mounted stun emitter, armored chassis â€” no augmentations to short, purely mechanical)

**INITIAL STATE** - Silence: cold (hamon cold blue, bank empty) â€” walked home, no engagement - Chorus: 4 rounds loaded (12-gauge standard) - Bio-battery: 72% â€” ate at Mrs. Chen's three hours ago, protein-heavy but not a full meal - Ballistic Precognition: passive and running

**ACT: WEST TOWN CROSS-STREET, 02:14**

The street smelled like rain on concrete and something burning two blocks over.

Kyle noticed the wrong heartbeat at the corner of West Erie and Ashland â€” too still, not pedestrian-still but waiting-still â€” and by the time he'd catalogued it, the NeoCortex had already found four more. One above. One behind a panel van. One behind the planter. One on the far side of the dumpster. All stopped. All breathing shallow. The array flagged the configuration in the fraction of a second it took him to keep walking without breaking stride.

An ambush. A good one, almost.

> Six positions. One elevated. They've done this before.

He kept his hands loose, his pace even, his eyes on the space between the parked cars where the van sat. He gave them ten more steps to commit.

They committed.

"Now."

Mira's voice. Chrome jaw catching the streetlight as she stepped out from behind the planter, machine pistol up. KT came out of the gap between the panel van and a sedan â€” augmented left arm fully extended, machete raised in her right. Rook materialized from the mouth of the parking structure at the end of the block. Dex came in from behind, footfall light, both handguns already drawn. And somewhere above, on the fire escape of the walk-up over the dry cleaner, Nines settled in.

Five humans. And then â€” a sound he hadn't catalogued yet â€” the scratching click of articulated legs on wet asphalt, and the dog rounded the dumpster.

Quadruped. Low-slung. Armored across the back and haunch. The jaw emitter left a faint ozone signature on the air when it activated. Pure machine â€” no BCI, no cardiac regulator, no augment signatures at all. The NeoCortex found nothing to read and moved on.

Kyle stopped walking.

"You're a long way from your contract territory," Mira said.

He didn't answer. His left hand crossed his body to the friction sheath across his back.

**[BEAT 1 â€” THE DRAW]**

The blade came across his inner left forearm on the way out â€” mune against the corundum strop, three full passes in the 0.4 seconds it took to complete the draw. The ferrocerium lit. Blue-white sparks scattered across his sleeve and died in the wet air. The hamon flickered from cold to a thin cyan thread â€” not much, but something.

> Not enough. Give it a fight.

Mira's finger moved toward the trigger.

The NeoCortex read it â€” micro-tremor in her forearm, barrel alignment shifting two degrees left to lead him â€” and Kyle was already stepping right when the burst went through the space where his center mass had been. He heard the rounds clip the car door behind him, ringing it like a dull bell.

Dex fired from behind at the same moment. Kyle read that one too â€” the angle, the trajectory â€” and dropped his shoulder as he turned, letting the round pass high. Two shooters. Two reads. Bio-battery cost was accumulating but the reads were clean at 72%.

KT reached him first.

She was fast. The augmented arm swung in a horizontal arc â€” chrome catching streetlight â€” and Kyle caught the blow on the flat of Silence's blade rather than the edge. The impact rang through the steel, through the shingane, through his wrists. The hamon brightened. A thin white line down the full length of the blade, still not full but feeding now.

> Good. Stand in. Let her hit you again.

He stayed in contact for exactly one more exchange â€” she brought the machete down from the right, he crossed the blade to catch it, another hard impact, another bright pulse in the hamon â€” before he moved the edge to her left wrist.

Passive disruption. Contact to the augmented arm's motor bus interface.

The arm went dead from the elbow down. KT made a sound like a circuit breaker tripping â€” a short, high exhale â€” and the chrome went limp. She stared at it for one full second with an expression that had no word in any language Kyle knew.

He stepped past her.

**[BEAT 1 STATE]** - Silence: hamon lit â€” ~35% charge, two hard parries - Chorus: 4 rounds (untouched) - Bio-battery: 68% â€” Ballistic Precognition 2 reads (âˆ’4%), active movement (+0%) - KT: augmented arm crashed, still standing, machete in right hand, stunned

**[BEAT 2 â€” THE DRAG]**

Rook had given up on a clean shot from the structure entrance and was closing, heavy pistol in a two-hand grip, trying to get inside Kyle's blade radius where the katana couldn't generate enough arc. Smart. Kyle gave him the approach and used the time.

He reversed his grip for half a step and dragged Silence across the hood of the sedan â€” full pressure, mune down â€” the length of the car. The TENG film caught. Sparks ran the full length of the drag, orange against the wet black metal, and the hamon jumped. The rain had muted the output â€” he could feel the resistance in the charge rate â€” but the drag still fed the bank. Not as fast as a dry surface. Fast enough.

The car hood was now scarred. A blade-width channel across the paint, bright metal underneath.

Rook fired at three meters. The NeoCortex read it â€” Rook's grip had telegraphed, the barrel was dropping with his step â€” and Kyle rotated his body out of the path, the round going between his arm and his ribs. He felt the pressure displacement. He kept moving.

From above: Nines. The fire escape. The rifle barrel dropping into Kyle's lane.

> The elevated threat. You've been letting him settle in.

"Nines, now!" Mira called.

Kyle moved before Nines's finger reached the trigger. He was already behind the sedan when the round punched through the window above him, glass coming down in a curtain. He crouched low, back against the wheel well, the hamon now a solid white-blue line in the dark.

Sixty percent. Maybe more.

--- [BEAT 2 STATE] - Silence: ~60% charge â€” drag on sedan hood plus two more clash-parries - Chorus: 4 rounds - Bio-battery: 64% â€” Ballistic Precognition continuous (âˆ’4%), Sensory Amplification ticked on briefly to locate Nines (âˆ’3%) - KT: regrouping, has her machete - Rook: 3 meters, closing - Nines: fire escape above, rifle - Dex: circling behind the sedan - The Dog: still on Mira's side, holding position

--- [BEAT 3 â€” THE DOG]

The dog came around the front of the sedan low and fast, articulated legs finding grip on the wet asphalt without slipping, jaw emitter live and glowing blue-white.

Kyle heard it before he saw it â€” the leg-click pattern had changed cadence, from patrol to approach â€” and he was moving up and onto the sedan's hood as the dog lunged for his ankle, the stun emitter discharging into empty air under his boot. The ozone hit him hard. He felt his back teeth vibrate.

No augmentation signatures. No interface point. The passive disruption layer on Silence's edge was useless against a machine with no electronics accessible from the outside. He'd have to open it up or go through it.

He went through it.

Chorus came off his hip in his left hand â€” the bird's-head grip filling his palm under the bore â€” and he put the first round into the dog's rear actuator housing from the hood of the sedan, two meters away, muzzle down.

The sound was enormous in the enclosed street.

The dog's rear legs collapsed. It hit the asphalt and slid, still trying to drag itself forward on the front pair, jaw emitter still cycling. Kyle dropped off the hood on the far side, putting the car between them.

"He shot Ripper!" â€” Dex, from somewhere behind the van.

Rook: "Don't stop! Don'tâ€”"

KT came around the planter at a sprint, machete overhead, one arm dead and useless at her side. She was screaming something that wasn't words anymore.

Kyle read her path, stepped inside the arc of the machete swing, and brought the edge across her throat at the point of closest contact.

It was precise. It was fast. The blade carried through the full motion and rang off the concrete planter on the follow-through â€” a hard, clean note in the night air.

*Clean. The kind of clean the people who built him would have liked.*

The machete hit the asphalt.

"He cut KT's head off, man!" â€” Dex, voice cracking. "He justâ€”he cut KT'sâ€”"

"Shut up!" Mira. Her voice was tight. Something had changed in the calculation she'd walked in with.

--- [BEAT 3 STATE] - Silence: ~75% charge â€” hard contact with concrete planter rang the blade clean, hamon bright white - Chorus: 3 rounds remaining - Bio-battery: 58% â€” Ballistic Precognition (âˆ’4%), one Neural Overdrive NOT activated (held in reserve) - KT: dead - The Dog: rear legs destroyed, front legs dragging it forward, jaw emitter still live â€” threat reduced, not eliminated - Rook: pulling back toward the structure entrance - Nines: still elevated, trying to reacquire - Dex: behind the van, voice cracking

--- [BEAT 4 â€” NINES]

The fire escape was the problem. Nines had elevation and patience and Kyle was out of covered positions on this side of the street.

He activated Augmentation Signature Read â€” 5% cost â€” and scanned upward. The array mapped Nines in 0.3 seconds: BCI implant behind the left ear, ocular enhancement on both eyes (Tier 2, civilian grade), no cardiac implant, dominant-hand cybernetic wrist brace for recoil stabilization. The wrist brace had an interface point at the inner forearm, below the palm. A cut there would take away Nines's ability to hold the rifle steady. The shot would go wide.

Kyle needed elevation.

He ran for the planter â€” concrete, two meters tall, dead tree branching at eye level â€” and went up the face of it fast, using the textured concrete, onto the branch, then a one-step up the decorative steel fence post above the planter and off into space.

Nines tracked him. The barrel moved.

Kyle read the trajectory in flight â€” the NeoCortex processing the micro-angle of the barrel in the half-second he was airborne â€” and twisted his body, the round going past his left side so close he felt it as heat. He caught the fire escape railing with his right hand, swung his legs up, got a foot onto the grating.

Nines had 1.2 seconds to react.

Kyle used 0.8.

The edge of Silence came down across Nines's right forearm at the wrist brace interface point. The disruption cascade hit the brace's motor control. Nines's hand opened involuntarily. The rifle dropped through the grating and fell three stories to the alley below.

Kyle kicked Nines off the fire escape landing and didn't watch him fall. He was already looking down at the street.

Dex had broken from cover and was running. South. Fast.

Kyle let him run.

--- [BEAT 4 STATE] - Silence: ~80% charge â€” the Nines contact was passive (no bank draw), hamon near-full sodium-white - Chorus: 3 rounds - Bio-battery: 49% â€” Augmentation Signature Read (âˆ’5%), Ballistic Precognition (âˆ’4%), sustained elevated movement compounding - KT: dead - The Dog: still dragging itself, front legs only â€” now a low-priority threat - Nines: disarmed, fell/dropped from fire escape - Dex: running south, not being pursued - Rook: structure entrance â€” has cover, heavy pistol - Mira: planter position â€” reassessing

--- [BEAT 5 â€” ROOK AND THE DOG]

The dog had dragged itself twelve meters while Kyle was on the fire escape. The jaw emitter was still cycling. It was six meters from where he'd land when he dropped back to street level.

He dropped.

The dog lunged from two meters and Kyle put his second Chorus round through the jaw emitter housing at point-blank range.

The stun system died. The dog's forward momentum carried it into his shin and he stepped over it, one hand touching the asphalt as he regained his footing, Silence raking across the street surface in the same motion â€” twenty centimeters of drag, sparks, not much charge but the hamon was already near-full and didn't need it.

The dog's legs cycled twice and stopped.

Rook fired from the structure entrance. Two rounds in a tight group. The NeoCortex read them both â€” Rook was good, controlled, the reads arrived late at 49% bio-battery but still arrived â€” and Kyle moved into the gap between the shots, letting them go past on either side of his body in a way that looked, to anyone watching, like something that should not be physically possible.

*Showing off. The hardware liked that. He hated when the hardware liked things.*

*No. Conserving rounds.*

He closed the distance to Rook at a run. Augmentation Signature Read had already mapped him â€” augmented legs, Tier 3, interface points at both hips where the femoral socket met the chassis. No cardiac implant. BCI at the right temple.

Rook swung the pistol to track him and Kyle got inside the barrel with the last two steps, the slide of the pistol pressing against his ribs as it fired â€” the round going into the concrete below his foot, the muzzle blast burning his shirt â€” and brought Silence's edge in a precise arc to Rook's right temple.

Passive disruption. BCI interface point.

Rook's eyes went blank. The pistol dropped from a hand that had forgotten it was holding something. He sat down on the concrete in the entrance of the parking structure, staring at nothing, every augmentation in his body simultaneously silent.

He was breathing. He would be breathing for a while. He would wake up with the worst headache of his life and no memory of the last six hours.

--- [BEAT 5 STATE] - Silence: ~85% charge â€” near-full hamon, sodium-white in the dark - Chorus: 1 round remaining - Bio-battery: 43% â€” Ballistic Precognition (âˆ’4% this beat), Augmentation Signature Read used on Rook (âˆ’5%) â€” WARNING: approaching 40% threshold - KT: dead - The Dog: destroyed - Nines: out of fight (fire escape) - Dex: gone south - Rook: downed, BCI crashed, conscious but blanked

--- [BEAT 6 â€” MIRA]

One left.

Mira hadn't run. He gave her credit for that.

She was standing in the open now, machine pistol at her side, pointed down. The chrome jaw caught the streetlight from the west. She was looking at the dog, at Rook in the structure entrance, at the place on the asphalt where KT's machete had landed.

"Fourteen of us jumped you in the Bucktown stretch two months ago," she said. "You walked out. We lost eight people."

Kyle said nothing. He let her talk.

"This wasn't a hit." She was looking at his face now, or trying to â€” he was still in shadow. "This was a test. I needed to see if the stories were true."

*The NeoCortex flagged her micro-expressions. She wasn't lying. He hated that the hardware was the thing that knew.*

"They're true," Kyle said.

The machine pistol came up.

He read the shot â€” Mira was good, the barrel was steady, the pre-fire indicators minimal â€” and he didn't dodge it.

He let it hit the subdermal mesh on his left shoulder. The round deformed against the woven lattice under the skin, the impact like a punch from someone heavy. He felt the bruise forming immediately. He kept walking toward her.

Mira's eyes went wide.

The hamon of Silence was sodium-white. Full. Casting a thin wash of light across the wet asphalt between them.

He stopped two meters away. Close enough that she could see the light it was making.

"Drop the weapon," he said.

She dropped it.

"Tell me who hired you for the test."

Mira told him. It took about forty-five seconds. The NeoCortex flagged zero deception indicators.

He left her standing at the planter, arms at her sides, looking at the street full of her crew. The dog's legs had stopped twitching. Rook was starting to come back â€” blinking slowly, hands moving on the concrete, trying to remember what hands were for.

Kyle picked up the length of West Erie without hurrying. The hamon cooled slowly as he walked, sodium-white to blue-white to the faint cold blue of a mostly-spent bank.

By the time he reached The Pivot, it was barely visible.

He took the stairs. He didn't sleep.

--- FINAL STATE - Silence: ~40% charge (passive drain walking home), hamon cold blue - Chorus: 1 round remaining â€” needs reload - Bio-battery: 38% â€” âš  below warning threshold, no active abilities available until he eats - Casualties: KT (dead), The Dog (destroyed), Rook (downed/blanked), Nines (disarmed/fell), Dex (fled) - Mira: standing, information extracted, released - Kyle: bruised left shoulder (round stopped by subdermal mesh), no serious injuries - The street: one scarred sedan hood, a blade channel in the asphalt from the drag, KT's machete still lying in the gutter, the dog's chassis fouling the lane
